Error 0x80200013 (BG_E_TOO_LARGE) occurs in the Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS), the component that handles actual file downloads for Windows Update. The queued job is larger than the BITS maximum job size setting, or a policy is restricting job size. This is sometimes seen after a WSUS admin tightens BITS quotas or after corruption in the BITS queue database.

The fix is to reset the BITS queue, check relevant group policies, and let Windows recreate the job at proper size.

causes.cause: Group Policy limiting BITS job size
Low free disk space on system drive

symptoms: bitsadmin /list shows jobs in TRANSIENT_ERROR state

fixSteps.title: Reset BITS queue
fixSteps.instruction: Elevated Command Prompt: net stop bits && del %ALLUSERSPROFILE%\Microsoft\Network\Downloader\qmgr*.dat && net start bits

fixSteps.title: Check BITS policies
fixSteps.instruction: gpedit.msc > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > BITS - set all to Not Configured on non-domain PCs.

fixSteps.title: Free disk space
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure at least 10 GB free on the system drive.

fixSteps.title: Re-run Windows Update
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Background Intelligent Transfer Service - the throttled file transfer component Windows Update uses to download content in the background.

faq.q: Does resetting BITS harm other apps?
faq.a: Some apps like Skype and OneDrive also use BITS and may need to redownload queued items, but data is not lost.

title: Windows Update Error - BITS Job State Invalid
shortDescription: A BITS transfer job is in an invalid state for the requested operation.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80200053 (BG_E_INVALID_STATE) is returned when Windows Update asks BITS to perform an operation (resume, complete, cancel) against a job that is no longer in a compatible state. This is typically a symptom of a crashed or orphaned BITS job, or qmgr.db corruption.

Resetting the BITS queue almost always restores normal operation. Persistent recurrence suggests a user-profile-specific BITS issue or a deeper service problem.

causes.cause: Orphaned BITS job from previous download attempt

symptoms: bitsadmin shows jobs stuck at TRANSIENT_ERROR
Updates do not restart after reboot

fixSteps.title: Cancel all BITS jobs
fixSteps.instruction: Elevated Command Prompt: bitsadmin /reset /allusers

fixSteps.title: Reset qmgr database
fixSteps.instruction: net stop bits; delete qmgr*.dat in %ALLUSERSPROFILE%\Microsoft\Network\Downloader; net start bits.

fixSteps.title: Re-register BITS service
fixSteps.instruction: sc config bits start= delayed-auto (then restart).

fixSteps.title: Run SFC and DISM
fixSteps.instruction: Repair any underlying corruption.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Sometimes. But if qmgr.db is corrupted, a simple restart will not help - the database must be deleted.
Any in-flight BITS-based downloads will need to restart.

title: Windows Update Error - Cannot Connect to Update Server
shortDescription: Windows Update cannot establish a connection to the update server.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80072EFD (WININET_E_CANNOT_CONNECT) is a WinHTTP/WinINet connectivity error. The Windows Update client tried to open a TCP connection to a Microsoft Update or WSUS server and failed. Causes are almost always network-layer: firewall blocks, proxy mis-configuration, DNS failures, or the server being unreachable.

The error is closely related to 0x80072EFE (connection aborted) but specifically indicates the connection could not be established at all.

causes.cause: Firewall blocking outbound traffic to update servers
DNS resolution failure for update hostnames
WSUS server offline in enterprise environment

symptoms: No connection could be made messages
Updates consistently fail at Checking for updates

fixSteps.title: Test basic connectivity
fixSteps.instruction: ping windowsupdate.microsoft.com and nslookup the same host to verify DNS and reachability.

fixSteps.title: Reset WinHTTP proxy
fixSteps.instruction: netsh winhttp reset proxy then netsh winhttp import proxy source=ie in an elevated prompt.

fixSteps.title: Flush DNS
fixSteps.instruction: ipconfig /flushdns

fixSteps.title: Disable VPN/proxy temporarily
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off any VPN client or proxy and retry Windows Update.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Similar but distinct: EFD means cannot connect, EFE means the connection was aborted mid-transfer.
Yes. Split-tunnel misconfiguration or VPN DNS can block access to Microsoft Update servers.

title: Windows Update Error - Authorization Cab Failed To Download
shortDescription: Windows Update failed to download or validate the authorization cabinet file.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80244004 (WU_E_PT_SOAPCLIENT_PARSE) is raised by the Patch Transport component (PT) when the SOAP client cannot parse the response from the update server. The response may be malformed due to a proxy rewriting it, an intercepting security appliance, or in rare cases a damaged server-side file on a WSUS installation.

Troubleshooting focuses on confirming the network path between client and update server is clean, and on validating the WSUS IIS application in enterprise environments.
symptoms: All WSUS clients on a network fail simultaneously

fixSteps.title: Verify direct access
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily remove WSUS policy and try Windows Update directly to Microsoft.

fixSteps.title: Check WSUS IIS
fixSteps.instruction: On the WSUS server, run wsusutil.exe checkhealth and review the IIS application pool.

fixSteps.title: Exclude WU hosts from TLS inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Ask IT to bypass *.windowsupdate.com from TLS interception.

fixSteps.title: Reset Windows Update components
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset sequence.

whenToCallPro: Contact your WSUS administrator if multiple PCs show this error simultaneously.

faq.q: Is this a client or server problem?
faq.a: When many clients report it at once, the WSUS server or network is at fault. A single client pointing to issues on that device.
SOAP is the XML-based protocol Windows Update uses to talk to update servers.

title: Windows Update Error - SOAP Client Failed to Initialize
shortDescription: The Windows Update SOAP client could not initialize.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80244008 (WU_E_PT_SOAPCLIENT_SOAPFAULT) indicates that Windows Update received a SOAP fault from the update server. The server explicitly returned an error rather than valid update metadata. On WSUS, the fault is often due to a database issue, disabled application pool, or expired certificate on the SSL binding.

In home scenarios, this error is usually transient and resolves by itself. Persistent reports typically trace back to an enterprise WSUS installation that needs server-side attention.
symptoms: Reported WSUS SOAP fault in WindowsUpdate.log
All clients fail at roughly the same time

fixSteps.title: Check WsusPool
fixSteps.instruction: On WSUS server open IIS Manager and confirm WsusPool is running.

fixSteps.title: Reindex SUSDB
fixSteps.instruction: Run the official WSUS SUSDB maintenance script via sqlcmd against the WID or SQL instance.

fixSteps.title: Verify SSL certificate
fixSteps.instruction: Check the binding for port 8531/443 and renew if expired.

fixSteps.title: Restart WsusService
fixSteps.instruction: net stop WsusService && net start WsusService on the server.

whenToCallPro: This is typically a server-side WSUS issue requiring the administrator.

faq.q: Can a client fix this alone?
faq.a: Usually no - the fault originates on the server.
Yes, and Microsoft recommends it monthly for WSUS performance.

title: Windows Update Error - Exceeded Maximum Server Round Trips
shortDescription: Windows Update made too many requests to the update server without completing.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80244010 (WU_E_PT_EXCEEDED_MAX_SERVER_TRIPS) appears when the Windows Update client exceeds the maximum number of allowed round trips to the update server while enumerating updates. Each round trip retrieves a subset of metadata; if the subset never shrinks the client gives up at a built-in threshold (typically around 100).

The usual trigger is a large backlog of superseded updates in a WSUS catalog or a client that is many cumulative updates behind. Installing a recent servicing stack and cumulative update manually collapses the metadata and fixes the issue.

causes.cause: Very outdated Windows build (many updates behind)
Bloated WSUS metadata with many superseded updates

symptoms: Update scan takes hours then fails
WindowsUpdate.log shows hundreds of PT round-trips

fixSteps.title: Install latest SSU + LCU manually
fixSteps.instruction: Download the most recent Servicing Stack Update and Latest Cumulative Update for your build from Microsoft Update Catalog.

fixSteps.title: Delete datastore.edb
fixSteps.instruction: net stop wuauserv; delete %windir%\SoftwareDistribution\DataStore\DataStore.edb; net start wuauserv.

fixSteps.title: WSUS admins: decline superseded updates
fixSteps.instruction: Run Server Cleanup Wizard to remove superseded content and shrink metadata.

fixSteps.title: Retry Windows Update
fixSteps.instruction: After installing latest SSU/LCU and restarting, run update scan again.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: A system more than a year behind cumulative updates often hits this limit.

faq.q: Do I need to decline superseded updates manually?
faq.a: The WSUS Server Cleanup Wizard handles it; running it quarterly is a good practice.

title: Windows Update Error - Server Did Not Issue Cookie
shortDescription: The update server did not issue a required authentication cookie.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80244011 (WU_E_PT_NO_AUTH_COOKIES_CREATED) means the Windows Update client could not obtain an authentication cookie from the update server. For Microsoft Update this should be automatic; for WSUS, cookie issuance depends on the ClientWebService ASP.NET application running correctly.

Resolution is usually server-side: restart the WSUS application pool, reset the ASP.NET state, or check that the SelfUpdate URL is reachable. On the client, resetting WU components can also force a fresh handshake.
symptoms: Self-update phase fails on all WSUS clients

fixSteps.title: Test ClientWebService URL
fixSteps.instruction: In a browser visit http://WSUS-SERVER:8530/ClientWebService/client.asmx - it should return WSDL XML.

fixSteps.title: Restart WsusPool
fixSteps.instruction: IIS Manager > Application Pools > WsusPool > Recycle.

fixSteps.title: Repair ASP.NET registration
fixSteps.instruction: aspnet_regiis.exe -i on the WSUS server may help if ASP.NET is misregistered.

fixSteps.title: Client: reset WU components
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset.

whenToCallPro: WSUS server-side action is usually required.

faq.a: WSUS uses a session cookie to correlate client state across multiple SOAP calls during a scan.

faq.q: Will clients recover automatically after fixing WSUS?
faq.a: Yes, the next scan cycle will issue a new cookie.

title: Windows Update Error - Client Received Duplicate Cookie
shortDescription: The Windows Update client received a duplicate authentication cookie from the server.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80244012 (WU_E_PT_REGISTRATION_NOT_SUPPORTED) indicates that the WSUS server is behaving in a way the client does not expect - typically issuing duplicate registration cookies or failing the new-registration handshake. It often appears alongside 0x80244010/0x80244011 during WSUS outages.

On the client side the remedy is to reset update components so that a clean registration occurs; server-side admins should verify IIS and WSUS service health.

causes.cause: Client ClientID lost or duplicated across imaged PCs

symptoms: PCs deployed from the same image all fail at once

fixSteps.title: Regenerate WU client ID
fixSteps.instruction: Elevated Command Prompt: reg delete HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate /v SusClientId /f && reg delete HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate /v SusClientIdValidation /f && wuauclt /resetauthorization /detectnow

fixSteps.title: Reset SoftwareDistribution
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset.

fixSteps.title: Verify WSUS health
fixSteps.instruction: wsusutil.exe checkhealth on the server.

fixSteps.title: Sysprep image updates
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure reference images clear SusClientId via sysprep or a first-boot script.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Cloning a Windows install without sysprep leaves multiple PCs sharing the same SusClientId value.
On modern Windows 10/11 it is superseded by UsoClient, but wuauclt /resetauthorization still functions for this purpose.

title: Windows Update Error - HTTP 400 Bad Request
shortDescription: Windows Update received an HTTP 400 Bad Request response from the server.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80244013 (WU_E_PT_HTTP_STATUS_BAD_REQUEST) maps directly to an HTTP 400 response from the update server. The client sent a request the server considered malformed. Typical causes are URL-rewriting proxies, outdated client software sending obsolete headers, or a WSUS server running an old servicing stack.

Both client-side (update WUA) and server-side (patch WSUS) remediation may be required.

causes.cause: Proxy rewriting request URLs or headers

symptoms: Only certain clients on a network succeed

fixSteps.title: Install latest SSU/LCU
fixSteps.instruction: Update the client to the newest available SSU/LCU.

fixSteps.title: Temporarily bypass proxy
fixSteps.instruction: netsh winhttp reset proxy to test direct connectivity.

fixSteps.title: Patch WSUS
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure WSUS role has latest cumulative updates; reboot the server after.

fixSteps.title: Reset WU components
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: The server understood the request was well-formed HTTP but rejected its content.
Yes, next-gen firewalls that inspect and rewrite HTTP content can cause 400s.

title: Windows Update Error - Language Pack Not Applicable
shortDescription: The requested language pack cannot be applied to this Windows installation.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80073715 (ERROR_SXS_XML_E_BADXMLDECL / lang-pack mismatch) occurs when Windows tries to install a language pack (LXP/LIP/CAB) that does not match the current OS build or edition. Language pack CABs are build-specific; a CAB from Windows 10 21H2 will not install on 22H2, for instance.

The fix is to obtain the matching language pack for your exact build, or to perform a feature update first so the language catalog is refreshed.

causes.cause: Language pack CAB does not match OS build
Corrupted CBS store preventing pack install
Attempted LP install on wrong edition (N/KN)

symptoms: Language install fails in Settings > Time & language
DISM reports 0x80073715 when adding LP CAB

fixSteps.title: Check Windows build
fixSteps.instruction: Run winver and note the build (e.g. 22621.xxxx).

fixSteps.title: Download matching language pack
fixSteps.instruction: Use Microsoft Update Catalog or VLSC to obtain the LP ISO that matches your build.

fixSteps.title: Install via DISM
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:path\to\lp.cab

fixSteps.title: Repair component store
fixSteps.instruction: If install still fails: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.q: Can I use a Windows 11 LP on Windows 10?
faq.a: No. Language packs are not forward or backward compatible across major versions.

faq.q: What about LXPs from the Microsoft Store?
faq.a: LXPs (Local Experience Packs) are delivered via the Store and auto-match your build.

title: Windows Update Error - Component Store Mismatch (FOD)
shortDescription: Features on Demand cannot be installed due to a component store mismatch.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F0905 typically occurs when installing a Feature on Demand (FOD) or optional component, such as Notepad, WordPad, the RSAT tools, or .NET Framework. The servicing stack detected that the requested component does not match what is available in the client's component store, often because the Windows Update source does not include the FOD payload.

Common scenarios: WSUS does not host FOD packages by default, the PC is offline, or group policy restricts the FOD source to Windows Update only while WSUS is configured.

causes.cause: WSUS does not host FOD packages
UseWUServer policy forcing FOD via WSUS

symptoms: Cannot install RSAT, OpenSSH client, or other FOD
Optional features show as Install failed

fixSteps.title: Allow direct FOD download
fixSteps.instruction: gpedit.msc > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Specify settings for optional component installation - check Download repair content... directly from Windows Update.

fixSteps.title: Install from ISO source
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Add-Capability /CapabilityName:... /Source:D:\sources\sxs pointing to mounted Windows ISO.

fixSteps.title: Repair component store
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.

fixSteps.title: Retry optional feature install
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Optional features > Add a feature.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Feature on Demand - optional components like language packs, RSAT, OpenSSH that are downloaded as needed.

faq.q: Why does WSUS not host them?
faq.a: FODs are delivered as Microsoft Store/FOD packages and must be fetched from Microsoft directly unless the admin syncs them specifically.

title: Windows Update Error - Feature Source Files Could Not Be Downloaded
shortDescription: Windows could not download the source files needed to enable a feature.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F0906 (CBS_E_SOURCE_MISSING) indicates the component store could not locate or download the payload required to enable an optional feature such as .NET Framework 3.5 or Hyper-V. By default, Windows downloads these payloads on demand from Windows Update; if the network is unavailable or WSUS blocks it, the operation fails.

Providing a local source via the /Source switch of DISM or Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature solves the problem in offline/WSUS environments.

causes.cause: No internet access during feature enable
Corrupted source CAB on install media

symptoms: Turn Windows features on or off fails for .NET 3.5
DISM output: error 0x800F0906 - source files could not be downloaded

fixSteps.title: Mount Windows ISO
fixSteps.instruction: Mount a matching Windows ISO, note drive letter (e.g. D:).

fixSteps.title: Install feature with /Source
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:NetFx3 /All /Source:D:\sources\sxs /LimitAccess

fixSteps.title: Bypass WSUS via GPO
fixSteps.instruction: Enable the Always contact Windows Update for repair content policy.

fixSteps.title: Check connectivity
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the PC can reach Microsoft Update servers if not using /Source.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.q: Does the ISO need to match the exact build?
faq.a: Ideally yes, especially for feature-update-aligned FODs, though .NET 3.5 sxs is fairly version-tolerant.
It tells DISM not to fall back to Windows Update, which is important in disconnected environments.

title: Windows Update Error - DISM Failed Due to Network Policy
shortDescription: DISM could not contact Windows Update to retrieve feature payload due to policy.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F0907 (CBS_E_GROUPPOLICY_DISALLOWED) is raised when a group policy specifically blocks DISM and the Component Based Servicing subsystem from reaching out to Windows Update for source files. It is a policy decision, not a failure.

The remedy is to either adjust the group policy, or provide an offline source using the /Source switch in DISM or the -Source parameter in PowerShell's Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature.

causes.cause: Policy: Specify settings for optional component installation disallows direct download

symptoms: Group Policy disallowed message during feature install

fixSteps.title: Review policy
fixSteps.instruction: gpedit.msc > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Specify settings for optional component installation and component repair.

fixSteps.title: Temporarily enable direct download
fixSteps.instruction: Enable the Download repair content... directly from Windows Update option.

fixSteps.title: Use offline source
fixSteps.instruction: Provide /Source pointing to sources\sxs on install media.

fixSteps.title: Contact IT
fixSteps.instruction: If policy cannot be changed, request an exception or WSUS FOD sync from IT.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.q: Will the policy be restored automatically?
faq.a: Yes, at the next gpupdate cycle domain policy will re-apply.
Allowing direct WU download for FODs is generally low risk, but enterprises may have reasons to block it.

title: Windows Update Error - Servicing Operation Failed
shortDescription: A Windows servicing operation for an optional feature failed.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F0908 is a generic servicing failure surfaced when enabling or disabling a Windows optional feature. It often accompanies a more specific inner error in CBS.log. Typical drivers are damaged package manifests in WinSxS, a pending reboot blocking new servicing actions, or insufficient disk space.

Inspecting CBS.log for the exact inner HRESULT is the most efficient way to narrow down the cause.

causes.cause: Insufficient disk space on system drive

symptoms: CBS.log shows inner errors such as 0x80073712

fixSteps.title: Reboot and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Restart the PC to clear pending operations and try again.

fixSteps.title: Inspect CBS.log
fixSteps.instruction: Open %windir%\Logs\CBS\CBS.log and search for the exact HRESULT near the failure.

fixSteps.title: Run DISM restore
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth followed by sfc /scannow.

fixSteps.title: Free disk space
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure at least 10 GB free on C:.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log (admin read access required).

faq.q: Is this always fixable on the client?
faq.a: Most instances are, but severe manifest damage may require an in-place upgrade repair.

title: Windows Update Error - Package Could Not Be Staged
shortDescription: Windows Update failed to stage an update package to the component store.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F0233 (CBS_E_STAGING_FAILED) occurs during the staging phase of Windows servicing - the step where CBS copies the update payload into %windir%\SoftwareDistribution\Download and verifies integrity against the manifest. Failures at this stage are most often caused by disk errors, antivirus interference, or exhausted space on the system drive.

Addressing disk health and freeing space usually resolves the error.

fixSteps.title: Check disk health
fixSteps.instruction: Elevated Command Prompt: chkdsk C: /scan then schedule /f /r if errors are found.

fixSteps.title: Disable AV temporarily
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off third-party real-time scanning, retry the update.

fixSteps.title: Free disk space
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure at least 15 GB free on C:.

fixSteps.title: Reset SoftwareDistribution
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset sequence.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: The step where an update is unpacked and verified before being committed to the component store.
A failing SSD can, if it returns bad sectors during staging. Check SMART attributes.

title: Windows Update Error - Servicing Package Manifest Corrupt
shortDescription: The manifest for a Windows servicing package is corrupt or invalid.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F0232 (CBS_E_UNEXPECTED_PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE or manifest corruption variant) indicates that CBS encountered a package whose manifest cannot be trusted. The most common scenarios are partial download, tampered signing, or a manifest architecture that does not match the OS.

Remediation focuses on replacing the bad payload with a freshly downloaded one and repairing the component store.

fixSteps.title: Reset SoftwareDistribution
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset sequence so payloads re-download cleanly.

fixSteps.title: Run DISM RestoreHealth
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.

fixSteps.title: Download update manually
fixSteps.instruction: Grab the KB from Microsoft Update Catalog and install via standalone installer.

fixSteps.title: In-place repair install
fixSteps.instruction: If corruption persists, do an in-place upgrade to refresh system manifests.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.q: Should I manually edit the manifest?
faq.a: No - manifests are signed and hand-editing invalidates them.
Run winver; if 64-bit you need the x64 package.

title: Windows Update Error - Update Requires Missing Payload
shortDescription: The update depends on payload files that are not present on the system.
fullDescription:
Error 0x800F024D indicates CBS detected a dependency whose payload files are missing from the component store. This typically happens when a prior update was cleaned up (for example via DISM /StartComponentCleanup /ResetBase) and removed files that a subsequent delta update expects to patch.

Restoring the component store from Windows Update or an install ISO brings the missing payload back. Using /ResetBase should be done sparingly for this reason.

causes.cause: Previous use of /ResetBase removed required payload

symptoms: CBS.log: source files could not be found for package

fixSteps.title: Run DISM with online source
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth

fixSteps.title: Use install media as source
fixSteps.instruction: Mount matching ISO and run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:wim:D:\sources\install.wim:1 /LimitAccess

fixSteps.title: In-place upgrade
fixSteps.instruction: Run setup.exe from ISO to refresh all payloads while keeping files/apps.

fixSteps.title: Avoid /ResetBase in future
fixSteps.instruction: Do not use DISM /ResetBase unless you are sure no delta updates are pending.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: It marks the current component versions as the new baseline, removing older superseded versions. This saves space but can break dependency chains.
Yes - use an ISO matching your Windows version for cleanest results.

title: Windows Update Error - Restart Required to Finish Update
shortDescription: The system requires a restart to complete a pending update installation.
fullDescription:
Error 0x8024A11C is a state indicator rather than a true failure: Windows Update is telling you that a prior update left the system in a state that requires a restart before any new updates can proceed. Until the restart is performed, further update operations will queue or fail.

Simply rebooting usually clears the state. If reboots repeatedly fail to finalize, Pending.xml or session.xml in the WinSxS store may be stuck, and manual cleanup is needed.
symptoms: Restart now banner in Settings > Windows Update

fixSteps.title: Restart (not Shut down)
fixSteps.instruction: Start > Power > Restart. Avoid Shut down which uses Fast Startup.

fixSteps.title: Disable Fast Startup
fixSteps.instruction: Control Panel > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > uncheck Turn on fast startup.

fixSteps.title: Clear stuck pending transaction
fixSteps.instruction: Boot into WinRE > Troubleshoot > Command Prompt: DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions

fixSteps.title: Run DISM/SFC
fixSteps.instruction: Post-reboot: repair component store.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.q: Why do I need to disable Fast Startup?
faq.a: Fast Startup resumes from a saved kernel state and does not fully process pending updates during shutdown.
Yes, rarely. WinRE cleanup with /RevertPendingActions can break the loop.

title: Windows Update Error - Hardware Not Supported for Windows 11
shortDescription: Windows Update determined the hardware does not meet Windows 11 minimum requirements.
fullDescription:
Error 0x8024A223 is surfaced by the Windows Update Agent when a client attempts a Windows 11 feature update but does not meet the published compatibility bar (CPU generation, TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage). Microsoft's compatibility appraiser returns a block verdict and WU refuses to offer the upgrade.

The correct response is to run the PC Health Check tool to see which specific requirement is unmet, enable TPM/Secure Boot in firmware if available, and consider hardware upgrades or staying on Windows 10.

causes.cause: CPU not on Windows 11 supported list

symptoms: Windows 11 not offered in Windows Update
PC Health Check reports unmet requirements

fixSteps.title: Run PC Health Check
fixSteps.instruction: Download from microsoft.com/windows/windows-11 and run Check now on the This PC tile.

fixSteps.title: Enable TPM 2.0
fixSteps.instruction: Enter UEFI firmware, look for PTT (Intel), fTPM (AMD), or Security Device Support and enable it.

fixSteps.title: Enable Secure Boot
fixSteps.instruction: In UEFI firmware, set Boot mode to UEFI (not Legacy/CSM) and enable Secure Boot. Convert MBR to GPT with mbr2gpt if needed.

fixSteps.title: Consider hardware upgrade or remain on Windows 10
fixSteps.instruction: If CPU is unsupported, upgrading via unofficial means is not recommended. Windows 10 is supported through October 2025.

whenToCallPro: Consult a professional if you are uncomfortable modifying UEFI firmware.

faq.q: Can I force Windows 11 on unsupported hardware?
faq.a: There are registry bypasses, but Microsoft warns such systems are not entitled to updates. Not recommended for primary PCs.

faq.q: Will my CPU ever be added to the list?
faq.a: Microsoft has expanded the list only minimally since launch. Do not count on it.

title: Windows Update Error - Catastrophic Failure
shortDescription: Windows Update reported a catastrophic failure that prevented any further processing.
fullDescription:
Error 0x8000FFFF (E_UNEXPECTED) is a generic catastrophic failure returned by many Windows subsystems, including Windows Update and the Microsoft Store. It means an unexpected state was encountered that could not be recovered. Among update scenarios it frequently appears after major servicing stack corruption, damaged user profile data, or severe registry damage.

Because the error is generic, diagnosis requires correlating event logs and CBS.log timestamps. Core remediation is an aggressive component repair cycle and, if needed, profile or in-place-upgrade recovery.

causes.cause: Bad sectors on the system drive
Date/time wildly incorrect blocking cert validation

symptoms: Random 0x8000FFFF anywhere in Windows (not just update)
Microsoft Store also fails with same code

fixSteps.title: Check date and time
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Time & language > Date & time - ensure Set time automatically is on and the time is correct.

fixSteps.title: Run DISM + SFC
fixSteps.instruction: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth then sfc /scannow.

fixSteps.title: Create new user profile
fixSteps.instruction: Create a local admin, sign in, and test Windows Update. If it works, migrate data and retire the old profile.

fixSteps.title: In-place repair
fixSteps.instruction: Run setup.exe from Windows ISO with Keep personal files and apps.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: If the clock is off by years, TLS certificates appear invalid and nearly every Microsoft service breaks.

faq.q: Is a full reinstall ever required?
faq.a: Rarely. In-place repair fixes most 0x8000FFFF cases without wiping data.

title: Windows Update Error - Update Service Expired
shortDescription: Windows Update metadata for this device has expired.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80248015 (WU_E_DS_SERVICEEXPIRED) occurs when the service registration for the Windows Update agent has expired. This is most commonly seen on devices whose system clock is incorrect, causing Windows to believe the update service metadata (which has an embedded expiry date) is out of date.

Correcting the system date/time and resetting update components almost always clears the issue.
symptoms: System time shows 2000 or other wrong year

fixSteps.title: Fix system clock
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Time & language > Date & time - enable automatic time. Or run w32tm /resync in elevated prompt.

fixSteps.title: Replace CMOS battery
fixSteps.instruction: If the clock drifts after every shutdown, replace the CR2032 motherboard battery.

fixSteps.title: Reset SoftwareDistribution
fixSteps.instruction: Standard reset.

fixSteps.title: Delete datastore.edb
fixSteps.instruction: net stop wuauserv; delete DataStore.edb; net start wuauserv.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Signed metadata has validity windows. A wrong clock makes everything look expired.

faq.q: How often should I replace CMOS battery?
faq.a: Every 5-7 years on average.

title: Windows Update Error - Interactive User Required
shortDescription: The update requires an interactively logged-in user to proceed.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80240020 (WU_E_NO_INTERACTIVE_USER) indicates Windows Update attempted to install an update that requires an interactive session, but no user was logged in. Some updates - notably those with EULA prompts or specific optional components - cannot be silently applied by the SYSTEM account during automatic maintenance windows.

The fix is to log in interactively and trigger the update manually, or configure group policy to allow automatic acceptance of EULA prompts if appropriate.

causes.cause: No user logged in during Active Hours install attempt
Scheduled task runs as SYSTEM without interactive rights

symptoms: Update stays in Pending install state indefinitely
Only some updates fail with this code

fixSteps.title: Sign in and install manually
fixSteps.instruction: Log in as a local user with admin rights and run Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates.

fixSteps.title: Enable auto-accept policy
fixSteps.instruction: gpedit.msc > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update > Manage updates offered from Windows Update > Enable features introduced via servicing that are off by default (as applicable).

fixSteps.title: Restart Windows Update service
fixSteps.instruction: net stop wuauserv && net start wuauserv

fixSteps.title: Check optional update list
fixSteps.instruction: Some drivers require manual selection in Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Some preview/optional packages, driver updates with vendor EULAs, and Edge-related preview builds.
No, it is by design for user-consent scenarios.

title: Windows Update Error - Invalid Windows Update Operation
shortDescription: Windows Update rejected the requested operation as invalid.
fullDescription:
Error 0x8024000E (WU_E_XML_INVALID) is raised when the Windows Update client parses malformed XML from metadata or configuration files. This can happen when a policy XML is corrupted, when a third-party tool modifies WU registry keys, or when datastore.edb contains inconsistent records.

Resetting the update cache and restoring registry defaults (on non-managed PCs) typically clears the error.

causes.cause: Malformed policy XML pushed by third-party tool

symptoms: Inconsistent update state (some work, some fail)

fixSteps.title: Reset SoftwareDistribution
fixSteps.instruction: Standard stop-rename-start sequence.

fixSteps.title: Delete WU policy keys
fixSteps.instruction: On non-managed PCs: reg delete HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /f

fixSteps.title: Run DISM/SFC
fixSteps.instruction: Repair component store and system files.

fixSteps.title: Check third-party utilities
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall third-party privacy/update blockers like O&O ShutUp or WUB.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Many leave the update stack in inconsistent states. Remove them before troubleshooting.

faq.q: Will deleting policy keys affect domain PCs?
faq.a: Yes - they will be re-pushed by AD. Do this only on home/personal PCs.

title: Windows Update Error - Cycle Detected in Update Metadata
shortDescription: Windows Update detected a circular dependency in update metadata.
fullDescription:
Error 0x8024000F (WU_E_CYCLE_DETECTED) is an uncommon metadata error where the update catalog describes a circular dependency - update A requires B, which requires A. In practice this occurs when metadata is partially downloaded, when two incompatible WSUS replicas are contacted, or when the client's datastore.edb is corrupt.

Clearing the metadata cache usually fixes it on the client side.

fixSteps.title: Delete datastore.edb
fixSteps.instruction: net stop wuauserv; del %windir%\SoftwareDistribution\DataStore\DataStore.edb; net start wuauserv.

fixSteps.title: Re-run Windows Update
fixSteps.instruction: Force a scan - metadata will re-download.

fixSteps.title: WSUS admins: resynchronize
fixSteps.instruction: Force a full sync on the WSUS server.

fixSteps.title: Run SFC and DISM
fixSteps.instruction: Repair underlying components if needed.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: No, datastore.edb only caches metadata.
Rare on Microsoft Update, more common with WSUS replica chains.

title: Windows Update Error - No Updatable Items
shortDescription: Windows Update did not find any updatable items during the scan.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80240024 (WU_E_NO_UPDATE) indicates the update scan completed but the server reported no applicable updates. In many cases this is benign - the system is fully up to date. However, when accompanied by the error being displayed to the user (rather than a green check), it suggests the scan scope was too narrow, a policy is filtering all updates, or the catalog failed to provide applicability data.

If you expect updates and see this code, review group policy and WSUS targeting.

causes.cause: System is genuinely up to date
WSUS computer group has no approved updates
Feature update deferral policy set very high

fixSteps.title: Verify with manual check
fixSteps.instruction: Go to Microsoft Update Catalog and check if any KB is newer than your installed build.

fixSteps.title: Review deferral policies
fixSteps.instruction: gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update > Manage updates offered - confirm deferrals are reasonable.

fixSteps.title: WSUS: verify approvals
fixSteps.instruction: Check WSUS console > Computers > your group > Updates approved for install.

fixSteps.title: Remove WU registry policies
fixSteps.instruction: On non-managed PCs, clear HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: Yes - a fully patched system routinely returns no applicable updates.

faq.q: What if I am on LTSC?
faq.a: LTSC receives security updates only; feature updates are not offered by design.

title: Windows Update Error - Update Commit Not Allowed
shortDescription: The post-reboot commit of a Windows update was not allowed.
fullDescription:
Error 0x80242016 (WU_E_UH_POSTREBOOTUNEXPECTEDSTATE) is raised when, after a reboot, the Update Handler finds the system in a state inconsistent with what it expected during the pre-reboot install. Typical triggers are third-party disk cloning or system-state-affecting tools running between the install and the reboot, damaged WinSxS Pending.xml, or aggressive antivirus blocking commit.

Repairing pending transactions and retrying the update from a clean boot normally resolves the issue.

causes.cause: Third-party tool modified system between install and reboot

fixSteps.title: Clean boot
fixSteps.instruction: msconfig > Services > Hide all Microsoft services > Disable all, then disable non-essential startup items in Task Manager. Reboot and retry the update.

fixSteps.title: Disable third-party AV
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily remove or disable third-party security software.

fixSteps.title: Revert pending actions
fixSteps.instruction: WinRE Command Prompt: DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions

fixSteps.title: Reset and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Reset Windows Update components and retry the update.

whenToCallPro: If troubleshooting steps fail and updates continue to fail.

faq.a: A startup mode that disables all non-Microsoft services and startup apps to eliminate interference.

faq.q: Is my AV really the problem?

title: Windows Update Error - HTTP 502 Bad Gateway

title: E_NOINTERFACE_UPDATE

fullDescription:
0x80004002 (E_NOINTERFACE) in WU context usually means a COM component (often the Windows Update Agent) is registered incorrectly. This can happen after an aborted upgrade or registry corruption.

title: WU_E_PT_HTTP_STATUS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
shortDescription: Windows Update received HTTP 408 Request Timeout from the server.
fullDescription:
0x8024401C is the WU mapping for HTTP 408. The server (typically WSUS) closed the connection because the client did not send the request fast enough.

Root cause is usually network instability or an overloaded WSUS.

fixSteps.title: Stagger client check-in times
fixSteps.instruction: Use detection frequency randomization in Group Policy.

fixSteps.title: Restart IIS WsusPool
fixSteps.instruction: On WSUS server, recycle the WsusPool app pool.

fixSteps.title: Retry on a wired connection
fixSteps.instruction: Wi-Fi packet loss commonly triggers 408 timeouts.
